subject: PeakShape renewal: staggered GPU provisioning and sizing plan
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@peakshape.ai>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
Cc: Kara Liu <kara@peakshape.ai>
Date: 2026-09-28T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: PeakShape renewal: sizing guidance for staggered provisioning

Hi Mateo,

We’re coming up on our renewal window and want to lock in dedicated capacity while smoothing spend across Q4. Usage has been spiky but trending up — we expect a steady growth in inference volume through the end of the year. Budget constraints mean we can’t take a full committed uplift up front; instead the procurement team has asked whether we can do a phased provisioning (smaller initial tranche, then a larger add in ~2-3 months).

Can Redwood propose a staging plan that balances cost and reliability? Specifically: a recommended starting GPU count, a target scale-up cadence, and any conservative buffers you’d recommend based on 90-day utilization. If you can share a draft SOW and provisional pricing for tranches that’d help speed procurement.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick 30-min call this week.

Samir
Head of ML Ops
PeakShape
[Attachment: PeakShape_usage_report.csv]
From: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>
To: Samir Patel <samir@peakshape.ai>, Kara Liu <kara@peakshape.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T08:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: PeakShape renewal: sizing guidance for staggered provisioning

Hi Samir / Kara —

Thanks for the note and the usage report. We can definitely structure a staggered provisioning that meets PeakShape’s budget cadence while keeping tail latency and throughput protected. Quick summary and ask: please confirm you shared the last 90 days of per-hour GPU utilization (the CSV), otherwise send peak-day traces and 95th p99 latency windows.

High-level proposal (draft, subject to the usage confirm):
- Tranche 1 (start Oct 15): 12 A100-equivalent GPUs (dedicated pool) for baseline throughput and a 15% headroom buffer for expected Q4 spikes.
- Tranche 2 (target: ~week 12 after Tranche 1): scale to +24 GPUs (total 36) if 30-day rolling utilization and request latency remain within agreed SLOs.
- Fallbacks: automatic overflow routing to a lower-cost burst pool during exceptional spikes; optional quantization recommendations (8-bit) we can pilot to reduce GPU footprint.

I’ve attached a provisional SOW and a pricing worksheet for tranche-level commitment and month-by-month billing options. Can we lock a 30-minute call to run through the plan tomorrow? I’ve cc’d Neha and Jordan from capacity planning — they’ll help validate the sizing numbers.

Attachments: [SOW_draft_v2.pdf], [provisional_pricing_tranches.xlsx]

Thanks,
Mateo Alvarez
Sr. Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference
From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>
To: Mateo Alvarez <mateo.alvarez@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan.blake@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-29T10:45:00-07:00
Subject: Internal: PeakShape utilization quicklook

Mateo / Jordan — quick internal summary after a light pass on the CSV Samir sent this morning: 

- 90-day aggregates: avg GPU utilization ~60% (weighted by active windows), 95th percentile node-level utilization ~88% on peak days.
- Concurrency: typical 18-22 concurrent inference workers during surge windows; top 5% of days show 35+ concurrent.
- Token distribution: median seq length small; however tail requests (~2% of tokens) push memory/KV cache pressure higher.

Recommendation (conservative):
- Offer Tranche 1 = 12 A100-equiv to start (protects baseline and small surges).
- Build explicit 15% buffer in Tranche 1 billing and operational plan (prefix caching + batching).
- Tranche 2 = +24 GPUs conditional on 30-day rolling utilization >= 70% sustained or repeated p95 latency breaches.
- Operational levers: enable KV prefix caching on high-frequency endpoints and enable medium-level quantization on non-critical models (estimated 15-20% GPU consumption reduction).

I can produce a short note with charts for the call if useful. From an ops standpoint we should avoid a single big jump — the staggered approach reduces risk and will let us time capacity provisioning to real consumption.

-Neha
Capacity Planning
Redwood Inference

Mateo —

Thanks — that plan looks reasonable and aligns with what procurement will approve. We’re fine to start with the 12 GPU tranche on Oct 15 and revisit in early January for Tranche 2. Please send a final SOW and DocuSign link; procurement has attached Purchase Order PO_4682.pdf as an initial commit for Tranche 1 pricing.

Two requests from procurement side: 1) a clear cancellation/scale-down clause for the phased commitment, and 2) a one-page appendix that lists which models/configs are eligible for quantization (for our internal compliance review).

If you can get SOW + DocuSign today we’ll route it and sign quickly.

Samir
